questions.title: Nature of the zona pellucida
questions.question: Regarding the zona pellucida, which of the following is correct?

options.A: It is formed mainly by the oocyte (with the granulosa cells)
options.C: It is traversed by microvilli projecting from the oocyte

explanations.A: Incorrect as a sole answer. The oocyte (together with the granulosa cells) does form the zona pellucida, but this is only one of several true statements.
explanations.B: Incorrect as a sole answer. The zona pellucida is indeed a glycoprotein coat (ZP1-3), but this alone is not the complete answer.
explanations.C: Incorrect as a sole answer. Oocyte microvilli do traverse the zona pellucida, but this is only one true statement.
explanations.D: Correct. The zona pellucida is a thick glycoprotein coat between the oocyte and the follicular cells, synthesised by both the oocyte and the granulosa cells and traversed by oocyte microvilli and corona radiata processes. All three statements are therefore true, which makes 'all of the above' the single best answer.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Because statements A, B and C are all true, 'none of the above' cannot be selected.

questions.learning_objective: State that the zona pellucida is a glycoprotein coat formed by the oocyte and granulosa cells.

questions.title: Follicular cells of the unilaminar primary follicle
questions.question: Unilaminar primary follicles are:

options.A: Present at birth as the only pre-pubertal follicle
options.B: Developing at puberty under the effect of LH
options.C: Containing a secondary oocyte with a haploid chromosome number
options.D: Surrounded by a single layer of cuboidal follicular cells

explanations.A: Incorrect. The follicle present at birth and before puberty is the primordial follicle, which has flattened follicular cells; the unilaminar primary follicle forms when those cells become cuboidal.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Early follicle growth to the primary stage is largely gonadotropin-independent; it is not driven by LH.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The primary follicle contains a primary oocyte arrested in meiosis I (diploid), not a haploid secondary oocyte.
explanations.D: Correct. The unilaminar primary follicle is defined histologically by a single layer of cuboidal follicular (granulosa) cells around the primary oocyte, in contrast to the flat cells of the primordial follicle. The zona pellucida also begins to appear at this stage. The change from flat to cuboidal cells marks the primordial-to-primary transition.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the flat follicular cells of the primordial follicle from the cuboidal layer of the primary follicle.

questions.title: Feature absent from the primary follicle
questions.question: The following structures are characteristic of a primary follicle EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Multilaminar primary follicles have several layers of granulosa cells, so this is a genuine feature.
explanations.B: Correct. The antrum is a fluid-filled cavity formed by coalescing follicular fluid (liquor folliculi) and it first appears in the secondary (antral) follicle. The primary follicle has granulosa layers, a zona pellucida and a developing theca but no antrum, so the antrum is the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A theca interna differentiates around the multilaminar primary follicle, so it is a true feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The zona pellucida appears in the primary follicle, so it is a true feature.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the antrum as the feature that defines the secondary follicle, not the primary.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.29 Dr Zahra answer table (Female Q17 = B); Q24 = B and Department Q30 = b (follicle with antrum = secondary) corroborate

questions.title: Layer separating the oocyte from the cumulus cells
questions.question: In a secondary follicle, the oocyte is separated from the follicular cells of the cumulus oophorus by the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The theca interna is a vascular, steroid-producing layer outside the granulosa basement membrane, not the layer next to the oocyte.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The zona glomerulosa is a zone of the adrenal cortex and has nothing to do with the ovarian follicle.
explanations.C: Correct. The oocyte is immediately surrounded by the zona pellucida, which separates it from the innermost follicular cells of the corona radiata and cumulus oophorus. The corona cells send processes through the zona to reach the oocyte, but the intervening layer is the zona pellucida itself. This is why the zona is the structure between the oocyte and the follicular cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The theca externa is the fibrous outer coat of the follicle, far from the oocyte.

questions.learning_objective: State that the zona pellucida separates the oocyte from the follicular cells in the secondary follicle.

questions.title: Origin of the corpus albicans
questions.question: Concerning the corpus albicans:

options.A: It appears in the fetal ovary
options.B: It develops from the corpus luteum

explanations.A: Incorrect. The corpus albicans is not a fetal structure; it forms after ovulation and luteal regression in the reproductive-age ovary.
explanations.B: Correct. When pregnancy does not occur, the corpus luteum degenerates and is replaced by fibroblasts and dense collagen, forming the white corpus albicans. It is therefore derived from the corpus luteum. Being an inactive scar, it secretes no hormones and is slowly resorbed.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The corpus albicans arises from the regressed corpus luteum, not directly from growing follicles.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The corpus albicans is fibrous scar tissue and has no secretory (estrogen-producing) function.

questions.learning_objective: State that the corpus albicans is the regressed, fibrosed corpus luteum.

field_notes.keySource: printed p.29 Dr Zahra answer table (Female Q11 = B); Q20 = A (corpus luteum becomes corpus albicans) corroborates
